extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Shared Task Dataset
extraction.description: A dataset for language-independent named entity recognition covering English and German. The dataset contains annotated text for four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations and miscellaneous entities. It includes training, development, test, and unannotated data files for both languages.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder, CNTS - Language Technology Group, University of Antwerp
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus consisting of Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For the training and development set, ten days' worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, the texts were from December 1996. The preprocessed raw data covers the month of September 1996. The German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English data: Reuters Corpus (Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997). German data: ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English data: Training and development from end of August 1996, test from December 1996, raw data from September 1996. German data: Training, development and test from one week at the end of August 1992, raw data from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created for this shared task. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories. This includes adjectives, like Italian, and events, like 1000 Lakes Rally, making it a very diverse category. The IOB tagging scheme originally put forward by Ramshaw and Marcus (1995) was used. Words tagged with O are outside of named entities and the I-XXX tag is used for words inside a named entity of type XXX. Whenever two entities of type XXX are immediately next to each other, the first word of the second entity will be tagged B-XXX in order to show that it starts another entity. Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping. When a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT tagger (for English part-of-speech tagging and chunking), Treetagger (for German lemmatization, tagging and chunking)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping. When a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset was designed for the CoNLL-2003 shared task on language-independent named entity recognition. The learning methods were trained with the training data. The development data could be used for tuning the parameters of the learning methods. When the best parameters were found, the method could be trained on the training data and tested on the test data. The challenge was to incorporate the unannotated data in the learning process.
